LESSON: GALLOPING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three
Subject: CREATIVE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Performing and Display
Topic 2.2: Galloping
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 14

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Galloping, part of Performing and Display in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade three CREATIVE ACTIVITIES.

Key inquiry question: Which animals use galloping movement?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Galloping together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Self-efficacy: learners: learner focuses on practising galloping skills by accepting feedback from peers.

• Communication and collaboration: The learner interacts with peers while playing games that involve galloping.

Values:
• Love: The learner portrays respect in providing positive feedback to peers during practise of galloping activity.

• Respect: The learner allows other chances while demonstrating galloping skills.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Social cohesion: The learner embraces own and others performance during practise of galloping.

Link to other subjects:

• Environmental activities: The learner learns about directions.

• Religious activities: learner learns positive values while providing feedback to peers.
